title: Please Waste My Time: Detection through Deception
location: Hybrid SandboxATL, 483 Moreland Ave NE, Third Floor, Atlanta, GA, US Red teamers rely on predictability; predictable enumeration paths, predictable credential locations, predictable network behavior. Deception defense exploits exactly that. This talk+workshop is a practical guide to wasting a red teamer's time, told by someone who has been on both sides of it. I've tripped honeypots mid-engagement. I've also built them. That dual perspective shapes everything in this session. We'll cover a tiered deception stack: Active Directory honey users and honey SPNs designed to catch Kerberoasting and lateral movement; canary tokens embedded in documents, file shares, and source code repositories; honey API endpoints and SSRF detection triggers for AppSec teams; and — newer territory — deception techniques purpose-built for AI systems, including canary instructions in LLM system prompts, honey documents in RAG pipelines, and fake AI API keys that alert when someone finds them. The talk includes hands-on exercises. Attendees will generate, plant, and trigger their own canary tokens during the session and leave with a working mental model for building a deception program, not just deploying a one-off trick.
